is up ~7% in premarket trading Monday after reporting phase 1b results for ALKS 7290 that indicated the novel orexin 2 receptor agonist performed well in a proof-of-concept study for ADHD.

The candidate was well tolerated in both healthy and ADHD patients. Also, at day 14, ADHD patients given ALKS 7290 showed dose-dependent, significant improvements on exploratory endpoints evaluating change from baseline on established clinical scales, the Adult ADHD Investigator Symptom Rating Scale (AISRS), and Clinical Global Impression-Severity Scale (CGI-S).
In the double-blind, placebo-controlled study, 50 ADHD participants were given ALKS 7290 doses of 20 mg, 50 mg, or placebo.
